## Natural history notes

A medium-sized band-winged grasshopper characterized by mottled gray, brown, and tan coloration that blends well with sandy soil, gravel, and dry vegetation, often with patterned wings flashed during short flights. In Florida, it is found in dry open habitats such as sandhills, scrub, pine flatwoods, roadsides, fields, and other sparsely vegetated sandy areas. It feeds mainly on grasses and other low plants, usually resting on bare ground where its camouflage is strongest and jumping or flying short distances when disturbed.
